neighbours.label: describing what a distributed computing system provides: replication, sharding, quorum, quotas, consistency
fire: Each write is acknowledged only after a majority of replicas agree, which keeps the cluster consistent.
The storage layer offers automatic partitioning, cross-region replication and failover.
Writes require a quorum of three nodes, so a single crash never loses data.
Administrators can assign per-tenant quotas so no team exhausts the shared cluster.
The cache is sharded across forty servers and replicated to guarantee availability.
Leader election ensures that only one node accepts writes at any moment.
The system synchronously mirrors every block to a second data center for durability.
Consensus between the replicas guarantees a single ordering of transactions.
quiet: Each essay is read by two teachers, who agree on a grade before it is returned.
The new phone offers a larger screen, a faster charger and a brighter camera.
Meetings require three board members, so a single absence never stops a vote.
Parents can assign weekly chores so no child does all the housework.
The bakery has forty branches across the country and sells bread at each one.
The election ensures that only one candidate becomes mayor at any moment.
The museum carefully photographs every painting before it is sent abroad.
Agreement between the partners decided the order of the projects.
